question: Does a different AVAudioSession mode record a table conversation on the iPad better than measurement mode?
answer: No evidence that it does. Measurement stays. Its low level did not hurt Apple's transcriber; what failed at the table was a person listening, so replay is now boosted instead.
decision: Operator stopped the experiment after round 1 on 2026-10-15 (round 2 would most likely confirm, not change, the outcome). Keep measurement mode; add a replay boost; spend the next test on speaker labels with a real two-person recording.

setup.device: iPad Air (5th generation), iPadOS 27.0, built-in microphone, research build spike/ipad-ink (PR #130)
setup.source: macOS 'say' voice Samantha reading the opening of the Gettysburg Address (103 words), played from a MacBook speaker a table's width away at Mac output volume 50
setup.transcriber: Apple SpeechTranscriber on the iPad, after Stop
setup.metric_order: word recall of the passage first, then speech minus noise (p90 minus p10 of 100 ms window levels); fixed before the takes
setup.content_policy: Levels and recall only. The Mac copies of the takes were deleted after scoring; the iPad copies expire under their 1-day keep period.

takes.result: stopped at 0:00: enabling voice processing reconfigured the microphone right after start, which the build read as a hardware change. Fixed in PR #131 (restart in place on the same input port); not re-run.

findings: The louder modes raised the noise floor about 20 dB but speech only about 15 dB, so speech stood out less than in measurement.
Recall hit its ceiling at volume 50: measurement and default both caught 98.1% of the words, so recall could not separate the modes at this level.
The session read-back showed the input gain is settable on this iPad and sits at 0.5. Whether raising it is analog (a real improvement) was not tested.
Measurement mode's low level is a listening problem, not a transcription problem: at -58 dBFS speech the transcript still caught 98% of the passage.
limits: One round: no closing measurement take, so no drift check.
A synthetic voice from one position at one volume; the quieter rounds (25 and 12) that could separate the modes on recall were not run.
Voice processing and full input gain were never measured.
replay_boost_check: ReplayBoost (added in the same change as this file) applied to the measurement take: +38.1 dB, speech -58.1 to -20.1 dBFS, background -37.9, peak -7.2, no samples near the ceiling, and AVAudioPlayer loaded the in-memory copy at full length (35.6 s).
